newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks edge higher after soft start.
newsitem.headline: French stocks edge higher after soft start.

text.p: French shares edged higher after a soft opening on Thursday, with the market nervous after overnight weakness on Asian markets and Wednesday's 50-point drop on the U.S. Dow Jones index.

Societe Generale's planned purchase of Credit du Nord from Paribas keeps merger interest alive. Rumours had been circulating recently over an acquisition in the financial sector although the names were vague.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 1.09 points or 0.05 percent at 2,332.71 at 0920 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down one at 2,335 from Wednesday's settle.

Societe Generale rises strongly on the back of news it in talks to buy Credit du Nord from Paribas. One trader said operators were probably buying back short positions on Societe Generale which had been taken out in the last few days on talk it could buy the CIC bank chain from insurer GAN.
But with a purchase of Credit du Nord, this was the lesser of two evils and made it less likely Societe Generale would acquire CIC.
"This is very good news for Paribas," the trader added.
Valeo eases after posting 1996 sales up 14.4 percent, in line with expectations.
Rhone-Poulenc continues weak on talk of a placement of stock in the market.

Alcatel Alsthom continues to strengthen, on a view it could benefit from a purchase of Thomson-CSF, contrary to previous fears any acquisition would be a burden. The government says it is still studying privatisation options for Thomson-CSF and has not decided between a public offer or private tender.
